Net Benefit for Dynamic Predictions under Left-Truncated and Right-Censored Data

tvNB.Rd

Computes estimates of the net benefit for a given decision threshold (decision_threshold) at a specified horizon time (Thoriz), using longitudinal information available up to a given starting time point (Tstart). The function supports joint models, Cox proportional hazards models and predictions obtained from any method. It provides inverse probability weighting and model-based estimation methods.

Usage

tvNB(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
tvNB(object, Time, event, LT_Time = NULL, Tstart,
     decision_threshold = NULL, Thoriz = NULL, Dt = NULL,
     type_weights = c("model-based", "IPCW"),
     preds_MB = NULL, name_model = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'jm'
tvNB(object, newdata, Tstart,
     decision_threshold = NULL, Thoriz = NULL, Dt = NULL,
     type_weights = c("model-based", "IPCW"), name_model = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxph'
tvNB(object, newdata, Tstart,
     decision_threshold = NULL, Thoriz = NULL, Dt = NULL,
     type_weights = c("model-based", "IPCW"), name_model = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

an object inheriting from class jm or coxph, or a numeric vector containing the dynamic predictions to be evaluated.

newdata

a data.frame that contains the longitudinal and covariate information for the subjects for which prediction of survival probabilities is required. If a jm object is used, the names of the variables in this data.frame must be the same as in the data.frames that were used to fit the linear mixed effects and the event process model that were supplied as the two first argument of jm. If a coxph is used it only applies to the event process. If the default method is used, the argument is not needed.

Tstart

numeric scalar denoting the time point up to which longitudinal information is to be used to derive predictions.

decision_threshold

numeric scalar between 0 and 1 denoting the decision threshold used in the net benefit.

Time, event, LT_Time

numeric vectors that must be specified when using the default method to compute the metric by directly using a vector of predictions, observed times (Time), the event indicator (event) and (possibly) left-truncated times (LT_Time).

Thoriz

numeric scalar denoting the time point for which a prediction of the survival status is of interest; Thoriz must be later than Tstart and either Dt or Thoriz must be specified. If Thoriz is NULL is set equal to Tstart + Dt.

Dt

numeric scalar denoting the length of the time interval of prediction; either Dt or Thoriz must be specified.

type_weights

character string denoting the type of weights to use to account for censorting. Options are model-based (default) and inverse probability weighting (using the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the censoring distribution, and adjusting for left truncation if necessary).

preds_MB

a numeric vector containing the model-based weights to be used for the individuals censored within (Tstart, Thoriz]. It must be specified when using the default method and the model-based estimator.

name_model

character string denoting the name of the model or object used for prediction evaluation; default is NULL, meaning that the name of the object in the environment will be used.

...

additional arguments passed to predict.jm().

Value

A list of class tvMetric with components:

metric

a numeric scalar denoting the estimated net benefit.

metric_type

the character string 'NB'.

nr

a numeric scalar denoting the number of subjects at risk at time Tstart.

nint

a numeric scalar denoting the number of subjects with an event in (Tstart, Thoriz].

ncens

a numeric scalar denoting the number of subjects with a censored time in (Tstart, Thoriz].

Tstart

a copy of the Tstart argument.

Thoriz

a copy of the Thoriz argument.

type_weights

a copy of the type_weights argument.

metric_info

a copy of the decision_threshold argument.

LT_MS

a logical that is TRUE if left-truncated times have been used.

classObject

the class of object.

nameObject

the name of the model; either a copy of the name_model argument, or the name of object.

References

Vickers, Andrew J and Elkin, Elena B (2006). Decision curve analysis: a novel method for evaluating prediction models. Medical Decision Making 26, 565–574.

Author

Arnau Garcia-Fernandez a.garciafernandez@erasmusmc.nl, Pedro Miranda-Afonso p.mirandaafonso@erasmusmc.nl and Dimitris Rizopoulos d.rizopoulos@erasmusmc.nl

See also

decision_curves, tvIWEC, tvEC, predict, jm

Examples

# \donttest{
# We fit a multivariate joint model
pbc2.id$status2 <- as.numeric(pbc2.id$status != 'alive')
CoxFit <- coxph(Surv(years, status2) ~ sex, data = pbc2.id)
fm1 <- lme(log(serBilir) ~ ns(year, 3) * sex, data = pbc2,
           random = ~ ns(year, 3) | id, control = lmeControl(opt = 'optim'))
fm2 <- lme(prothrombin ~ ns(year, 2) * sex, data = pbc2,
           random = ~ ns(year, 2) | id, control = lmeControl(opt = 'optim'))

jointFit <- jm(CoxFit, list(fm1, fm2), time_var = "year", n_chains = 1L)

# Net benefit with decision threshold 0.3, prediction horizon 7
# and landmark time 4
tvNB(jointFit, newdata = pbc2, Tstart = 4, Dt = 3, decision_threshold = 0.3,
     cores = 1L)
#> 
#> Accuracy Metric for the Joint Model 'jointFit'
#> 
#> Estimated Net Benefit with decision threshold 0.3: 0.0892
#> At time: 7
#> For the 225 subjects at risk at time 4
#> Number of subjects with an event in [4, 7): 34
#> Number of subjects with a censored time in [4, 7): 62
#> Accounting for censoring using model-based weights
#> 

# Considering the Cox model and IPW approach for estimation:
tvNB(CoxFit, newdata = pbc2.id, Tstart = 4, Dt = 3, decision_threshold = 0.3,
     type_weights = "IPCW")
#> 
#> Accuracy Metric for the Cox Model 'CoxFit'
#> 
#> Estimated Net Benefit with decision threshold 0.3: -0.0016
#> At time: 7
#> For the 225 subjects at risk at time 4
#> Number of subjects with an event in [4, 7): 50
#> Number of subjects with a censored time in [4, 7): 46
#> Accounting for censoring using 
#> inverse probability of censoring Kaplan-Meier weights
#> 


# Considering the vectors with predictions, observed times, event indicator and
# left-truncated times. We use the default method:
pbc2.id$lt <- runif(nrow(pbc2.id), 0, pbc2.id$years)
sfit0 <- summary(survfit(CoxFit, newdata = pbc2.id), times = 5)
sfit <- summary(survfit(CoxFit, newdata = pbc2.id), times = 5 + 3)
predictions <- 1.0 - (as.matrix(sfit$surv)[1L, ] / as.matrix(sfit0$surv)[1L, ])
tvNB(predictions, pbc2.id$years, pbc2.id$status2, pbc2.id$lt, Tstart = 5, Thoriz = 8,
     type_weights = "IPCW", decision_threshold = 0.25)
#> 
#> Accuracy Metric for the predictions 'predictions',
#> 	observed times 'pbc2.id$years', event indicator 'pbc2.id$status2'
#> 	and left-truncated times 'pbc2.id$lt'
#> 
#> Estimated Net Benefit with decision threshold 0.25: 0.0261
#> At time: 8
#> For the 125 subjects at risk at time 5
#> Number of subjects with an event in [5, 8): 33
#> Number of subjects with a censored time in [5, 8): 44
#> Accounting for left truncation and right censoring using 
#> 	nonparametric inverse probability weights
#> 

# Now, we consider the default method, but using the model-based estimator:
ind_censoring <- pbc2.id$years > 5 & pbc2.id$lt < 5 & pbc2.id$years < 8 & pbc2.id$status2 == 0
sfit2_8 <- summary(survfit(CoxFit, newdata = pbc2.id[ind_censoring, ]),
                 times = 8)
sfit_cens <- summary(survfit(CoxFit, newdata = pbc2.id[ind_censoring, ]),
                     times = pbc2.id$years[ind_censoring])
preds_MB <- rep(NA, length(pbc2.id$years))
preds_MB[ind_censoring] <- 1.0 - (as.matrix(sfit2_8$surv)[1L, ] / as.matrix(sfit_cens$surv)[1L, ])
tvNB(predictions, Time = pbc2.id$years, event = pbc2.id$status2, LT_Time = pbc2.id$lt, 
     Tstart = 5, Dt = 3, type_weights = "model-based", preds_MB = preds_MB, 
     decision_threshold = 0.3)
#> 
#> Accuracy Metric for the predictions 'predictions',
#> 	observed times 'pbc2.id$years', event indicator 'pbc2.id$status2'
#> 	and left-truncated times 'pbc2.id$lt'
#> 
#> Estimated Net Benefit with decision threshold 0.3: 0.0124
#> At time: 8
#> For the 125 subjects at risk at time 5
#> Number of subjects with an event in [5, 8): 33
#> Number of subjects with a censored time in [5, 8): 44
#> Accounting for left truncation and right censoring using 
#> 	model-based weights
#> 
# }
